extracted.intended_audience: war correspondents and general newspaper readers (AP newswire audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural rules for correspondents filing news dispatches from the Korean War zone, plus civilian/military regulations reported in the dispatches. Covers submission procedures, security-check policy, censorship guidance, and wartime civilian movement orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of field dispatches to 8th Army PIO
rubrics_metrics.description: News dispatches from the field must be submitted to the 8th Army Public Information Office to be transmitted over the Signal Corps teletype to Tokyo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories were required to be handed to the 8th Army PIO for transmission; this is a procedural requirement for sending copy from Korea to Tokyo. (Text: 'NEWS DISPATCHES FROM THE FIELD MUST BE SUBMITTED TO THE 8TH ARMY PIO TO BE TRANSMITTED OVER THE SIGNAL CORPS TELETYPE AT TOKYO.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Security-check policy (optional checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories would not be checked for security unless the correspondent specifically asked for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondents may request security checks; they can voluntarily submit teletype or telephoned stories for security review to protect against unintentional violations. (Text: 'BUT THE STORIES WOULD NOT _ BE CHECKED FOR SECURITY UNLESS THE CORRESPONDENT SPECIFICALLY ASKED FOR IT.' and 'REPORTERS WERE TOLD THEY COULD VOLUNTARILY SUBMIT THEM FOR SECURITY CHECKS IF THEY WISHED.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone submission and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The 8th Army would check copy that correspondents in Korea telephone to Tokyo if newsmen so desire; telephone connections with Tokyo were promised daily between specified hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone time would be divided among many correspondents; plan transmissions within the provided window (noted as between 2 a.m. and 4 a.m. local / corresponding EST times). (Text: 'THE 8TH ARMY ALSO SAID IT WOULD CHECK COPY THAT CORRESPONDENTS IN KOREA TELEPHONE TO TOKYO==IF NEWSMEN SO DESIRE.' and 'TELEPHONE CONNECTIONS WITH TOKYO WERE PROMISED DAILY BETWEEN 2 A.M. AND 4 A.M.')

rubrics_metrics.name: No formal censorship requirement (policy change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondents covering the Korean War no longer have to submit their stories for a security check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects a change in administrative policy: while formal prior censorship was removed, other restrictions and guidance (see other criteria) remained in force. (Text: 'CORRESPONDENTS COVERING THE KOREAN WAR NO LONGER HAVE TO g or THEIR STORIES FOR A SECURITY CHECK.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on criticism of command/allied soldiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism of command decisions or of the conduct of allied soldiers on the battlefield will not be tolerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum warned correspondents that criticism of command decisions or allied soldiers' conduct could lead to disciplinary action. This is framed as a reporting constraint and a security/disciplinary standard. (Text: 'CRITICISM OF COMMAND DECISIONS OR OF THE CONDUCT OF ALLIED SOLDIERS ON THE BATTLEFIELD WILL NOT BE TOLERATED.' and 'NEWSMEN FAILING TO COMPLY...WOULD BE SUBJECT TO “DISCIPLINARY ACTION.”')

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid publishing information that aids the enemy
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondents were urged to observe security regulations and avoid writing anything which might give aid and comfort to the enemy or hinder the effort of United Nations forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the absence of formal censorship, journalists were explicitly asked to self-police and avoid operational details or other information that could be helpful to enemy forces. (Text: 'OBSERVE SECURITY REGULATIONS AND * AVOID WRITING ANYTHING WHICH MIGHT GIVE AID AND COMFORT TO THE ENEMY OR HINDER THE EFFORT OF UNITED NATIONS FORCES.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction to prevent enemy learning helpful information
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondents were asked by General MacArthur's Headquarters and the PIO to prevent North Koreans from learning helpful information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specific security admonition: avoid transmitting details that would let the enemy learn positions, movements, or vulnerabilities. (Paraphrase of: 'ASKED CORRESPONDENTS TO PREVENT NORTH KOREANS FROM LEARNING OR HELPFUL INFORMATION.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilians must travel by special trains
rubrics_metrics.description: All civilians must travel by special trains (order for clearing villages likely to fall in the battlezone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of an evacuation/clearance proclamation to keep highways open for military traffic and concentrate civilian movement onto controlled rail transport. (Text: '1--ALL CIVILIANS MUST TRAVEL BY SPECIAL TRAINS.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted civilian liberty hours and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: All civilians in the war zone will be allowed two hours daily liberty and must remain in their homes at all other times; police, war supply workers, doctors, nurses and others directly connected with the war effort are exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A curfew/controlled-movement rule intended to reduce infiltration and protect military lines while exempting essential personnel. (Text: 'D-CATL CIVILIANS IN THE WAR ZONE WILL BE ALLOWED TWO HOURS DAILY LIBERTY AND MUST REMAIN IN THEIR HOMES AT ALL OTHER TIMES…POLICE, WAR SUPPLY WORKERS, DOCTORS, NURSES…ARE EXEMPTED.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict investigation of group movements
rubrics_metrics.description: All civilians, when making a group movement, must undergo strict investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group movements are treated as potential security risks and require screening before being permitted. (Text: 'SccALL CIVILIANS, WHEN MAKING A GROUP MOVEMENT, MUST UNDERGO STRICT INVESTIGATION.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Stragglers must carry authorized identification
rubrics_metrics.description: All stragglers from the army must carry authorized identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures to prevent infiltration by enemy agents posing as displaced persons or soldiers; stragglers without ID are suspect. (Text: 'h--ALL STRAGGLERS FROM THE ARMY MUST CARRY AUTHORIZED IDENTIFICATION.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for violating civilian regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: All those found violating these regulations will be considered enemies and will be executed immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extreme enforcement measure stated in the proclamation as the penalty for breaches of movement and identification orders. (Text: '5=--ALL THOSE FOUND VIOLATING THESE REGULATIONS WILL BE CONSIDERED ENEMIES AND WILL BE EXECUTED IMMEDIATELYe')
